body: The example checks a constant-state perfect material on prescribed Minkowski spacetime and calculates the energy density measured by a boosted observer. It is an exact solution of the adopted local matter balances on the fixed background, not a coupled Einstein solution or empirical report.

This page adopts a fixed-composition smooth perfect-fluid material model with an explicit local state function, perfect stress, conserved marker current, and local balance equations. It derives the local Gibbs and parcel first-law identities from the adopted state function, then records entropy advection and a restricted material-loop circulation law. The latter deductions remain conditional on the inspected draft mathematical suppliers [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-carter-circulation]]; their current readiness records identify stale MC01 input hashes. No universal equation of state, material applicability, PDE existence, or empirical observation is claimed.

The companion constructs and checks one homogeneous Minkowski solution of the selected bulk-relaxation model inside a declared near-equilibrium regime. Its entropy production follows conditionally from the A-page theorem, with the theorem's mathematical supplier assumptions carried through. No observation or material measurement is reported.

This page adopts two restricted constitutive branches: first-order gradient dissipation and a bulk-only relaxation model with a corrected extended entropy current. The first theorem derives the quadratic local production identity for sufficiently regular solutions of the first-order branch. The bulk theorem consumes the exact conditional identity of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] and verifies one homogeneous solution within a declared near-equilibrium regime. Both arguments retain their mathematical supplier assumptions; neither proves general solution existence, causal or stable evolution, or universal material behavior. No experiment is reported.

The example verifies explicit perfect-branch sound waves and spatially constant neutral modes. It shows by direct substitution why energy contraction does not imply that every perturbation decays. The comparison is conditional on the perfect-branch theorem and its stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis; it contains no empirical data.

This page adopts two adiabatic first-variation systems about a uniform rest state on prescribed Minkowski spacetime: a perfect-material branch and a bulk-relaxation branch. It proves global linear stability and finite propagation by applying the exact current mathematical suppliers conditionally, including their stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption. The causal parameter ranges, exact supplier hypotheses, SI conventions, and lack of a nonlinear error or existence claim are stated explicitly. No empirical observations are used.

This companion verifies an explicit underdamped periodic Cattaneo mode by direct substitution. Its temperature-departure envelope decays and a sufficiently small nonzero amplitude keeps the forward-time model state inside the selected near-equilibrium domain with positive temperature. The construction is a model calculation, not an experiment or a claim about measured transport coefficients.

This page adopts two distinct effective branches. The supported-rest Cattaneo subsystem uses constant positive heat capacity, conductivity, and relaxation time, together with a specified quadratic entropy; its entropy production, characteristic speed, and finite propagation are conditional model deductions, and relativistic causality requires the derived speed bound. The separate entropy-only radiation model adopts its own equation of state and perfect-stress balance; it yields local entropy-current conservation and a frozen Minkowski-rest sound speed of $c/\sqrt3$. Neither branch asserts a measured material realization, a universal constitutive law, or a microscopic quantum derivation.

The companion gives a finite softened two-body canonical instance, a point-particle collapse counterexample in a finite box, a confined Kepler energy with negative Gibbs-volume capacity and nonnegative canonical response under distinct preparations, and a constant-lapse gas normalization. These are exact examples within the stated models; none reports an observation or asserts that a physical system attains the model preparation.

This page develops three explicitly different finite model preparations: a softly regulated finite Newtonian canonical gas, a confined relative Kepler model under canonical and Gibbs-volume microcanonical conventions, and a finite ideal gas on a prescribed static relativistic background. The model assumptions are kept separate from the mathematical normalization and response results. Every response claim retains its preparation, entropy convention, regulator, and physical applicability limits; no result here asserts thermalization, an observed gravitational system, or generic self-consistent gravitational stability.

The examples specialize the A-page results to half compactness and to a half-capacity finite bath, and exhibit the divergence of central pressure as the constant-density compactness approaches its family endpoint. The star calculations remain within the specified constant-density model; the bath calculation remains within the adopted scalar exchange law. They report no measurement, generic compactness bound, causal fluid dynamics, or stability property of a relativistic star.

This page develops a static, isotropic, spherically symmetric $\Lambda=0$ Einstein-fluid model with a supplied smooth positive equation of state. The metric, areal radius, stress tensor, signature, curvature convention and SI quantities are stated explicitly. The local TOV result uses the current mathematical center-construction and Einstein-reduction suppliers conditionally; it claims no global stellar surface or generic stability.

The constant-density branch is a separate constitutive and boundary preparation. Its explicit regular solution and vacuum match hold only for $0<u<8/9$; this does not assert a general Buchdahl theorem or a causal finite-sound-speed EOS. The entropy item uses a separately supplied compatible local state chart and fixed mass-energy/particle constraints. It proves first-variation criticality only, not an entropy maximum or existence theorem. The finite-bath result is another selected effective model: a negative-capacity finite subsystem coupled to a logarithmic bath by a scalar exchange ODE. None of these model deductions is an observation or a claim that nature realizes the preparation.

The companion considers one ideal finite-region case: when the entropy-current flux vanishes on every side face, the conditional balance reduces to nondecreasing proper slice entropy, with equality when local production also vanishes. It is a thought experiment within the stated model, not an observation, horizon-area law, or global generalized second law.

These examples compute the exact lapse, local temperature, and observer acceleration in the Schwarzschild exterior, the Rindler right wedge, and a rigidly rotating Minkowski domain. Each uses the selected Killing flow and stays inside its timelike domain. The rotating quantum trace check is restricted to the cited one-mode model; it is not a continuum-field theorem. No horizon, Hawking, Unruh, or reported experimental temperature is inferred.

This page adopts one selected comoving stationary bath, derives its conditional Tolman–Ehrenfest temperature relation, and records two separate particle-exchange protocols before deriving the conditional Tolman–Klein relation. It also defines one finite, normalized classical Jüttner preparation from the exact mass-shell measure and partition supplier. The conclusions carry their stated connected-domain, positive-temperature, full-mass-shell or finite-cell hypotheses. They do not assert universal equilibrium, a generic curved-spacetime Gibbs/KMS state, collisional equilibration, or empirical material validity.

This page adopts one specified finite independent-cell Gibbs/KMS state in the selected stationary bath, derives the local proper-time KMS width orbit by orbit, and applies the exact finite-cell response theorem to neutral observables and finite controls. The state is an actual finite construction within the model assumptions; it does not assert a generic curved-spacetime Gibbs trace, equilibration dynamics, or an experimental realization. The response predictions keep the finite-time remainder, spectral lines, and zero-frequency qualification.

The cosine example gives a closed-form decaying mode in the supported parabolic heat model. Its redshifted temperature tends to a constant, while its proper-temperature limit varies with a nonconstant lapse. The formula and insulated-face conditions are verified directly; this constructed solution is not an experimental observation.

This page adopts one fixed-background, supported static heat branch with a positive lapse, constant heat capacity, conductivity proportional to the inverse lapse, insulated rectangular faces, and compatible positive data. It specifies the state function, heat flux, energy balance, no-local-power support, and entropy current. A conditional physics theorem consumes the exact mathematical static-heat solution and derives energy conservation, entropy increase, and relaxation of redshifted temperature to a constant. These statements remain conditional on the model assumptions; they do not establish empirical realization, a full Einstein-fluid solution, causal relativistic-fluid dynamics, or finite propagation speed.

This companion constructs the zero-spin, zero-charge member of the selected
stationary family and verifies its exact SI area-work differential. It records
a conditional model calculation, with no measurement or physical-process
claim.

This page adopts the smooth equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model with a
restricted null energy condition, proves the corresponding area increase for
a future-complete smooth null congruence with persistent compact cuts, and
converts the Kerr–Newman stationary-family identities to SI units. Each
conclusion retains its exact smoothness, energy-condition, domain, and
normalization assumptions.

The parameter map from selected SI inputs to the geometric family is
$$\Xi(m_*,J,Q_e)=\left(\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\frac{J}{m_*c},\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}Q_e\right).$$
Let $\mathcal P_{\rm SI}$ be the set of triples $(m_*,J,Q_e)$ with
$m_*>0$ and with the components $(m,a,q)=\Xi(m_*,J,Q_e)$ satisfying
$m^2>a^2+q^2$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the strict mathematical family of
[[prop-tgr-kn-first-law-smarr]]. Define
$\mathcal H_{\rm geom}:\mathcal P\to\mathcal D_{\rm geom}$ by the
geometric horizon tuple $(A_H,\kappa_{\rm KN},\Omega_{\rm KN},\Phi_{\rm KN})$
of that supplier; $\mathcal D_{\rm geom}:=\mathbb R^4$ records those four
components with units $(\mathrm{m^2},\mathrm{m^{-1}},\mathrm{m^{-1}},1)$
under the selected physical parameter map. Define
$\mathcal H_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P_{\rm SI}\to\mathcal D_{\rm SI}$ by the
SI tuple $(A_H,\kappa_{\rm acc},\Omega_{\rm SI},\Phi_{\rm SI})$ of
[[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]], where $\mathcal D_{\rm SI}:=\mathbb R^4$
has component units $(\mathrm{m^2},\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}},\mathrm{s^{-1}},\mathrm V)$.
The conversion map is
$$C^{-1}(A_H,\kappa_{\rm acc},\Omega_{\rm SI},\Phi_{\rm SI})=(A_H,\kappa_{\rm acc}/c^2,\Omega_{\rm SI}/c,\alpha\Phi_{\rm SI}/c).$$

The diagram states the equality
$\mathcal H_{\rm geom}\circ\Xi=C^{-1}\circ\mathcal H_{\rm SI}$;
the item proofs establish the component formulas, and no proof relies on the
diagram.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal P_{\rm SI} \arrow[r,"\Xi"] \arrow[d,"\mathcal H_{\rm SI}"'] &
\mathcal P \arrow[d,"\mathcal H_{\rm geom}"] \\
\mathcal D_{\rm SI} \arrow[r,"C^{-1}"'] & \mathcal D_{\rm geom}
\end{tikzcd}
```

This page adopts a one-dimensional exponential-coordinate chiral-current model and a separate massless Minkowski-vacuum acceleration model with explicit two-state rate rules. The reduced reference temperature follows conditionally from the contour spectrum and the adopted rate equation; the local proper-temperature comparison requires a separately selected stationary bath and a matched reference. The acceleration theorem uses the constructed temporal field smearing, states the finite-switch coefficient bound, and keeps its effective temperature distinct from an exact all-order detector probability or an observed reading.

This companion computes the entropy difference between two positive-mass
Schwarzschild members of the selected model family. The calculation is
conditional on the area-calibration theorem and cancels its undetermined
additive entropy constant; it is neither a measurement nor a microscopic
state-count argument.

This page adopts a restricted reversible-heat identification for the selected
strictly subextremal stationary family. Its conditional theorem combines the
exact SI family differential with the reduced exponential-current reference
temperature, explicitly identified with the same selected horizon generator.
The result fixes the area coefficient within that model while leaving the
entropy zero free; it asserts no general Hawking law or microscopic state count.

This companion gives one exact half-mass cutoff calculation inside the stipulated fixed-reference effective-emitter model. It is a conditional thought experiment, not a reported observation; the positive cutoff avoids any conclusion about the zero-mass endpoint.

This page combines a zero-mode-excluded ideal photon Gibbs/ray model with a restricted Schwarzschild stationary-family entropy input and an adopted fixed-asymptotic-reference mass balance. The positive-cutoff mass ODE, coarse entropy export, and internal quasistatic diagnostic are exact conditional model results. The diagnostic is not an error bound against an exact Einstein–quantum backreaction solution; the effective area is not a material patch on the null horizon, and no Hawking-collapse theorem, measured flux, or universal generalized second law is claimed.
